note: The contract for moving the four known-leak groups of tests/data/layer_leak_allowlist.json to python-hwpx-automation. Nothing has moved yet. The owner chose compatibility option A: every affected core name keeps working through 6.x, warns in the next major and is removed in the major after it. Releases are named only relative to each other; no version number or date is promised here.

groups.title: Official-document reference rules
coreKeeps: hwpx.diff_paragraphs and hwpx.doc_diff over documents, paths, text and paragraph sequences
reading a document's paragraph texts (the source dispatch other than the document-plan branch)
publicReplacement: MCP tool inspect_reference_consistency, routed to the automation owner

groups.title: Automation document-plan interpretation
coreKeeps: doc_diff and the reference check accept documents, paths, text, paragraph sequences and {"paragraphs"}/{"text"} mappings
publicReplacement: an automation function that turns a document plan (sections/blocks/children, heading/paragraph/table rows) into the paragraph sequence core takes
automation comparison and reference-check entry points call it before handing paragraphs to core
coreSurfaceAffected: the {"sections": ...} input branch of hwpx.doc_diff and hwpx.inspect_reference_consistency (stable names; the branch is behaviour, not a name)

groups.title: Report heading guessing in Markdown export
coreKeeps: hwpx.tools.markdown_export.export_markdown and HwpxMarkdownConverter: text, tables, images, notes, and headings read from recorded document structure
a genre-neutral hook through which a caller supplies its own heading detector (a callable from paragraph text to a Markdown heading or None)
publicReplacement: the report heading rule (Roman 'Ⅰ.' -> '#', Arabic '1.' under 40 characters -> '##') as an automation detector passed into export_markdown
automation Markdown export entry points pass it explicitly
coreSurfaceAffected: HwpxMarkdownConverter where it reaches the same detector
automationConsumers: hwpx_automation.handlers.read_export (document ingest: DocumentIngestor.default() reaches HwpxMarkdownConverter with detect_headings on)

groups.title: Evaluation-plan caption cleanup
coreKeeps: a byte-preserving primitive that removes text a caller selects from the trailing run of a table's wrapper paragraph, never crossing a paragraph or table boundary, through the same open-safety finalize path
publicReplacement: the '(N) short word' selection rule as an automation predicate passed to that primitive from office.evalplan

sequence: 1. Automation adds each replacement owner and switches its consumers; core is unchanged and still answers old callers.
2. Core adds the genre-neutral primitives (heading-detector hook, caller-selected trailing-text removal) in a minor release; the old names delegate to them with today's rule.
3. In the next major, every affected core name and behaviour emits a DeprecationWarning that names its automation replacement (compatibility.schedule).
4. In the major after it, the release that removes a core name also removes its allowlist/undetected entries and this group; the layer leak guard then fails if the pattern comes back.

schedule.6.x: Every affected core name and behaviour keeps working without a warning. Automation replacements ship and the neutral core primitives may be added in minors; the old names delegate to them with today's rule.
schedule.nextMajor: Every affected core name and behaviour emits a DeprecationWarning naming its automation replacement; output does not change.
schedule.majorAfterNext: The core names and behaviours are removed with their allowlist/undetected entries; only the neutral primitives stay in core.

compatibility.appliesTo: every name and behaviour listed under coreSurfaceAffected, stable or module-level
compatibility.policy: docs/stable-api.md: a stable name breaks only at a major boundary, after a DeprecationWarning in an earlier major

options.summary: Keep every core name working through 6.x; warn in the next major; remove in the major after it.
Warn from a 6.x minor once the automation replacements ship; remove in the next major. Needs an explicit exception to the stable-name policy for the two stable names.
Never remove: freeze the core copies as compatibility code without feature work and keep the allowlist entries.
